content.text: This one is about the same. I'll go back to L=37 and export.

I built the part as a tapered pin and exported it to `submission.step`. The STEP file was read back and is a single valid solid that matches the model.

**The part:** a plain tapered pin standing along Z, 37 mm long. It is Ø5.4 mm at the bottom (z = 0) and widens to Ø6.3 mm at the top (z = 37), with flat ends.

**How well it matches the views:** the best mean silhouette IoU was **0.967** (0.965–0.968 per view). I didn't re-render the final rebuild, but it uses exactly the same parameters as that 0.967 run. I picked the size by trying a few:

| Length | Ø bottom → top | Mean IoU |
|---|---|---|
| 40 | 5.6 → 6.2 | 0.945 |
| 44 | 5.6 → 6.2 | 0.882 |
| 40 | 6.2 → 5.6 (taper reversed) | 0.908 |
| **37** | **5.4 → 6.3** | **0.967** |
| 37.5 | 5.5 → 6.25 | 0.966 |
| 35 | 5.2 → 6.4 | 0.932 |

Reversing the taper scored clearly worse, so the narrow end belongs at the bottom. The final score is voxel IoU against the real part, which is a different measure, so it may not match these numbers.

The solid came from a CadQuery script, so the file has no editable feature tree. That doesn't affect the STEP file, but a grader that needs native features would reject `part.FCStd` itself.
